priya: Quick q — for per-key token buckets, how do we size capacity for short 1-5s spikes vs steady-state throttling? We're seeing ~200 qps bursts for <3s from a telemetry client that should be allowed, but sustained >50 qps should be throttled. Any rules of thumb?

 tom: I'd lean two-layer: tiny fast bucket for microbursts + a steady leaky limiter. Example math: base_rate = 50 r/s, burst_window = 3s => capacity = base_rate * burst_window = 150 tokens. Refill at base_rate/sec so short 200 qps for 1s ok, but sustained >50 gets limited. Config sketch: ```yaml
limiter:
  token_bucket:
    rate: 50
    capacity: 150
  leaky:
    leak_rate: 50
    max_queue: 20
```

eric: Heads up — per-key buckets for many keys mean memory and bookkeeping. Prefer per-org buckets as primary; create per-key buckets lazily and evict after idle TTL (e.g., 60s). Also cap per-key capacity so one key can't steal whole node.

 sasha: Another approach: EWMA smoothing to separate short spikes vs sustained traffic. Use a short window (10s) EWMA to track 'effective rate' and only trigger sustained throttle when EWMA > threshold. Combine with token bucket for instantaneous bursts. Pseudocode: ```if tokens>0: allow elif ewma_rate < base_rate: allow else: throttle```

 jake: For observability we should surface: burst_credit, ewma_rate, tokens_consumed, throttle_count, last_dropped_ts. Per-key sampled metrics + per-org aggregates. That will help tune capacity and TTL.

 aj: Rollout plan idea: canary 1% with these metrics: drop_rate, p99 latency, queue_saturation. If drop_rate spikes unexpectedly, flip to "soft" mode that returns 429 with Retry-After header and logs customer id for follow up. Also consider priority tags so critical customers bypass shared pool.

 tom: :thumbsup: Agree on TTL eviction + per-org primary. Also suggest a shared burst pool on the instance to absorb tiny keys instead of allocating a full per-key bucket.

 eric: What do we return when quota is exhausted — 429 or 503? My vote: 429 (rate-limited). For internal infra calls we could expose a circuit-breaker header and optionally return 503 for retries upstream.

 priya: Action items: 1) prototype two-layer limiter in staging + add ewma and burst_credit telemetry 2) Console: show "burst credits" % + ETA to refill per-key (sampled) and per-org 3) 1% canary next Tue, rollback if p99 latency + drop_rate exceed thresholds. I'll mock UI.

 deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout started for limiter-v2 -> staging (build 4821) :rocket:

 sasha: I'll PR a prototype with unit tests for EWMA detection and TTL eviction. Will include integration test for capacity/cold-start behavior.

 jake: I'll wire dashboards: per-org burst_credit_gauge, ewma_rate_histogram, sampled per-key traces. Ping me when PR is up.

 priya: Thanks everyone :heart: I'll drop the design notes into the repo and follow up in #eng-platform with concrete numbers from staging after the canary runs.
